items.headline: Claude Code Now Takes "Mods" So You Can Change How It Behaves and Looks
items.summary: Anthropic added mods to Claude Code: small TypeScript add-ons (a few lines of code, or Claude can write one for you) that change how it acts, customize its screen, or add features. You install them through the /plugin command in the terminal or desktop app.
items.why_it_matters: If you use Claude Code to build small tools or automations, you can now add guardrails (like blocking risky commands) or personal touches without waiting on Anthropic, and you can just ask Claude to build the mod for you.

items.headline: OpenAI Launches "Dots," Always-On AI Agents That Work Through ChatGPT, Slack and Teams
items.summary: At its DevDay event, OpenAI introduced dots: AI agents (programs that carry out tasks for you) that each get their own cloud computer and browser and can reach thousands of apps. You give one a goal, set what it may do on its own, and it brings results back for your review.
items.why_it_matters: This is the 'assistant that works while you sleep' idea aimed at everyday workers; it's rolling out to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium plans, so it's worth watching if you're deciding where to spend your AI budget.

items.headline: OpenAI's New GPT-6.1 Sol Costs One-Fifth as Much as Its Flagship Model
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol, a cheaper model that comes close to its top GPT-6 Astra on coding and computer-control tasks. Developers pay $2 per million input tokens (roughly 750,000 words) and $10 per million output tokens, about 80% less than Astra.
items.why_it_matters: Cheaper AI usually flows down to the apps and automations small businesses already pay for, so expect more capable tools at lower prices, and it's a good moment to compare what you're paying now.
